cards.title: Pocket Park Board Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only warm-up for a family table, tutoring table, or classroom writing center: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Set out the pretend porch-light card, one pencil, and a small paper display board for made-up story work: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Choose one tiny message for the board, then write what a character does after reading it: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: Front: The pretend porch-light turns on beside the pocket-park board when the message says: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: Back: The small print on the board gives one surprising detail: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: Story signal: A character reads the paper signal and decides to bring: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: When the pocket-park board glowed on the card, the reader saw, ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision: Add one word that makes the board message clearer: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Point to the signal and write one whisper-sized clue: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Retell the pocket-park message and add one new helper: ____________________.

cards.title: Spoon Ferry Lunchbox Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only sequence practice for a silly lunchbox harbor scene: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Place the card near paper lunch tokens and name the spoon ferry as a pretend tabletop boat: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Put three lunch tokens in order, then write how the ferry captain follows the signal: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: Front: Draw or name the first lunch token the spoon ferry picks up: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: Back: The pretend porch-light pattern tells the next stop is for: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: Story signal: The ferry must carry three tiny lunch items in this order: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The spoon ferry tapped the lunchbox dock and the captain called, ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision: Add a middle step that makes the lunchbox harbor trip easier to follow: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number three tiny items without speaking: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Tell the spoon ferry sequence with a new snack clue: ____________________.

cards.title: Acorn Errand Office Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only helper practice for a family, tutoring, or classroom writing table: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Set out three paper errand slips and one pretend porch-light card for an invented office scene: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Pick an office helper and one acorn task, then write how the helper reads the pretend signal: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: Front: The pretend porch-light card points to the helper badge labeled: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: Back: The errand office file asks for one missing object: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: Story signal: The helper sees a paper signal and chooses to carry: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: At the Acorn Avenue errand office, the signal blinked for ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision: Add one kind action the helper takes before the errand ends: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle a helper cue and write one object name: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Share the errand office problem and the helper solution: ____________________.

cards.title: Seed Library Question Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only question-making practice using a fictional seed library and paper room: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Place four paper seed labels around a table page and keep every label invented: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a question that the seed librarian must answer before the story can move on: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: Front: The pretend porch-light card marks the seed drawer with this question: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: Back: The paper room card answers with one tiny clue: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: Story signal: Before choosing a seed packet, the librarian asks: ____________________.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: In the seed library room, a paper light blinked over the question, ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision: Add one reason the question matters to the story plan: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write a question mark clue on the blank card: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Ask your seed-library question, then answer it with one new clue: ____________________.

cards.title: Rain Gauge Railway Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only sound-word practice for a family, tutoring, or classroom writing table: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Set out paper rail tiles, a pretend rain gauge label, and the porch-light card for a fictional railway scene: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Choose a sound for the pretend gauge, then write how the railway keeper interprets it: ____________________.
cards.signalFrontPrompt: Front: The pretend porch-light card shines next to the rain gauge sound word: ____________________.
cards.signalBackPrompt: Back: The railway card explains what that sound means in the story: ____________________.
cards.storySignalPrompt: Story signal: When the gauge goes ____________________, the tiny train must change its plan.
cards.firstLineSignal: First line: The paper rain gauge clicked twice, and the railway keeper said, ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision: Add one sound detail before the keeper makes a choice: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write a soft sound cue without saying it aloud: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Repeat the rain-gauge sound and add one new railway idea: ____________________.
